course_name_en: Specialization 1: Energy Technology and Energy Systems
prerequisites: Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Induction and Orientation Phase)

learning_outcomes.text: To name the basic functioning and designs of thermal and hydraulic fluid machines and classify them in the context of energy conversion.
To describe central thermodynamic concepts of selected energy conversion processes (e.g., power plant processes, heat pumps, refrigeration systems).
To explain the principles of energy turnover, efficiencies, and key figures in fluid machines and thermal systems.
To present typical components, designs, and applications of thermal systems in a structured way.
To explain basic approaches for modeling and numerical simulation of energy systems and thermal processes.
To explain simple relationships between energy generation, storage, and utilization in industrial energy systems.
To conceptually classify advanced energy technologies (e.g., geothermal, biomass, solar thermal, hydrogen technologies, thermal energy storage).
To independently acquire content, prepare it in a structured way, and apply it in related subject areas.
To discuss problems in small groups and jointly develop reasoned qualitative solution approaches.
To present results on selected technologies and concepts in an audience-appropriate manner.
To argue evidence-based positions on technological concepts, application limits, and efficiency potentials.
To clearly and comprehensibly document technical concepts and content from the topics of the specialization modules.
To recognize the importance of industrial energy systems and energy technology plants for society, environment, and economy and explain them using concrete technological examples.

syllabus_topics: Overview of the Energy Engineering specialization and its integration into Mechanical Engineering
Fundamentals of thermal energy conversion and selected power plant processes
Introduction to industrial energy systems and their components
Basic modeling approaches for energy systems and thermal processes
Energy generation, storage, and utilization in industrial energy systems
Functionality, designs, and applications of thermal and hydraulic fluid machines
Energy turnover, key figures, and efficiencies of turbines, pumps, and compressors
Typical components and designs of thermal systems
